title: Neuroendocrine tumors — gastroenteropancreatic
subtitle: Managed on two axes: differentiation (well-differentiated NET vs poorly differentiated NEC) and grade (Ki-67 / mitotic count) · then modified by primary site and whether the tumor is functional
source: Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Neuroendocrine Tumors (GI section) · AJCC 8th · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter

blocks.heading: WHO classification
blocks.footnote: Grade is the higher of Ki-67 or mitotic count. Poorly differentiated = neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC); well differentiated = NET. Well-differentiated G3 is a distinct sub-group — well-differentiated histology with Ki-67 >20%, and its behavior varies widely. It is not the same as NEC. Mixed neuroendocrine + adenocarcinoma = MANEC. “Carcinoid” is the older term for NET.

blocks.heading: Gastric NET types
rows: Autoimmune atrophic gastritis; elderly, female, pernicious anemia
Solitary nodule >1.5 cm, healthy gastric mucosa; usually symptomatic
blocks.footnote: Type applies to gastric NETs only. Check gastrin at baseline and on follow-up for gastric primaries.

blocks.heading: Site-specific points
items: Frequency: GI tract > lung > other. Most are sporadic; a minority arise in MEN1/MEN2
Small bowel: the classic carcinoid-syndrome primary (with lung); consider resecting the mesenteric mass prophylactically to avoid future complications
Pancreatic: broadest baseline hormone panel; sunitinib is approved here only; CAPTEM and temozolomide data are in pancreatic G1–G2
Carcinoid syndrome: small bowel and lung primaries with elevated serotonin — flushing is the archetypal functional symptom. If the tumor is functional, somatostatin analogue therapy is indefinite
† Telotristat and carcinoid crisis are not addressed in this chapter
Staging follows AJCC 8th by primary site (stomach, small bowel/ampulla, pancreas, colon/rectum)

boxes: there is no role for adjuvant therapy in NETs
small bowel: also resect the mesenteric mass
octreotide LAR 30 mg IM or lanreotide 120 mg SQ
But G3 NET is not NEC

blocks.heading: Regimens & dosing
rows: capecitabine 750 mg/m² PO BID d1–14 + temozolomide 200 mg/m² PO d10–14
5-FU 1200 mg/m²/day CIV 48 h + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² d1
capecitabine 850 mg/m² PO BID d1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² d1
cisplatin 60 mg/m² d1 + etoposide 100 mg/m² d1–3
carboplatin AUC 5 d1 + etoposide 100 mg/m² d1–3
ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6wk + nivolumab 240 mg q2wk
blocks.footnote: Pre-medicate temozolomide with ondansetron 8 mg PO 30 minutes prior. Temozolomide-containing regimens are typically capped at ~12 months.

blocks.heading: Workup — imaging & genetics
items: Multiphasic CT or MRI; for liver metastases, MRI with Eovist may help
Ga-68 DOTATATE PET at baseline, then every 2 years, or for a specific clinical question — not a routine restaging scan
Endoscopy as indicated
Brain MRI only for poorly differentiated disease with symptoms or raised suspicion
MR spine for symptoms, or considered annually for axial bone metastases
Genetics referral if diagnosed <50 years, family history suggesting MEN1/MEN2, or a somatic NGS finding with germline implications (BRCA1/2, MEN1, Lynch genes)

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — biochemical workup, trial evidence, monitoring and caveats

blocks.heading: Biochemical workup by site
rows: Chromogranin A · gastrin · glucagon · insulin/proinsulin · NSE · pancreatic polypeptide · VIP · 24-h urine 5-HIAA. As indicated: PTHrP, ACTH, GHRH
Chromogranin A, NSE, and only those elevated at baseline
Chromogranin A · NSE · 24-h urine 5-HIAA · gastrin if gastric primary
blocks.footnote: All serum labs preferably fasting; metastatic follow-up interval is usually q1–3 months as clinically indicated. Follow only the markers that were elevated at baseline.

blocks.html:
24-hour urine 5-HIAA requires a 3-day serotonin-restricted diet, before and during collection. Avoid: bananas, plums, pineapple, kiwi, avocado, eggplant, tomato products, nuts (especially walnuts), coffee, tea and chocolate.

Medications to avoid where feasible: cough and antihistamine preparations, antihypertensives, fluorouracil, MAO inhibitors, acetaminophen, aspirin, melphalan — weigh risks and benefits before stopping anything essential.

blocks.heading: Monitoring on therapy
items: On somatostatin analogues: check vitamin B12, vitamin D and TSH at least annually
SSA adverse effects: injection-site pain, abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, gallstones, hyper- or hypoglycemia, pancreatic exocrine insufficiency
Everolimus: stomatitis, rash, fatigue, diarrhea, infection, elevated lipids, pneumonitis
Sunitinib: diarrhea, nausea, fatigue, stomatitis, rash
Cabozantinib: hypertension, fatigue, diarrhea, hand-foot syndrome, thromboembolic events

blocks.heading: Trial evidence
rows: octreotide — TTP 14.3 vs 6 mo vs placebo (Rinke, JCO 2009)
Lu-177 dotatate, 2nd line+, G1/G2 — PFS not reached vs 8.5 mo; 2018 update median OS NR vs 27.4 mo (Strosberg, NEJM 2017)
Lu-177 dotatate first line, high-risk SSTR-positive G2–G3 GEP-NET — PFS 22.8 vs 8.5 mo vs high-dose octreotide. Not yet FDA approved (Singh, Lancet 2024)
Lu-177 edotreotide vs everolimus, G1/2 GEP-NET — PFS 23.9 vs 14.1 mo; OS trending favorable, not yet significant
cabozantinib — extrapancreatic PFS 8.4 vs 3.9 mo; pancreatic 13.8 vs 4.4 mo (Chan, NEJM 2024)
everolimus, pancreatic — PFS 11.0 vs 4.6 mo (Yao, NEJM 2011)
everolimus, non-functional GI/lung — PFS 11.0 vs 3.9 mo (Yao, Lancet 2015)
pancreatic NET only — PFS 11.4 vs 5.5 mo (Raymond, NEJM 2011)
pancreatic G1/G2 — PFS 23.2 mo vs temozolomide alone 15.1 mo (Kunz, JCO 2022)

blocks.heading: Pearls & caveats
items: Grade is the higher of Ki-67 or mitotic count — not an average, and not Ki-67 alone
Well-differentiated G3 is not NEC. Same Ki-67 threshold, different disease, and behavior varies widely
There is no role for adjuvant therapy in NETs — resect and observe
Sunitinib is pancreatic-only. CAPTEM and temozolomide data are also pancreatic G1–G2. Cabozantinib is the one with both pancreatic and extrapancreatic data
Ga-68 DOTATATE PET is not a routine restaging scan — baseline, q2 years, or a specific question
Follow only the tumor markers that were elevated at baseline
NETTER-2 (first-line PRRT in G2–G3) is not FDA approved yet; COMPETE's OS is not yet significant
† The chapter is GEP-NET focused — lung/bronchial carcinoid, thymic NET and pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma are separate entities not covered here
